title: Quantum Channel-Induced Geometry of the Uhlmann Phase in Qubit Systems
authors: F. Nieto-Guadarrama, F. Rojas, J. Villavicencio, Jesús A. Maytorena
abstract: We show that a cyclically controlled non-coherence-generating channel supplies a two-parameter family of closed Bloch trajectories, absent in the single-parameter (temperature) cycles of the thermal Uhlmann literature, whose associated Uhlmann phase develops a genuine vortex--antivortex structure on the channel-parameter torus. A qubit prepared in a pure state, which carries no geometric phase of its own, acquires a nontrivial Uhlmann phase, obtained here in closed form, purely from a closed loop in the space of the native quantum channel parameters. The net topological charge of these defects is constrained to zero by the Poincaré--Hopf theorem. As the input-state orientation approaches its critical values, the defects merge and annihilate in pairs following a square-root coalescence law. This defect dynamics drives local geometric transitions, a mechanism that contrasts with single-parameter thermal Uhlmann transitions, where a global quantized winding jumps as a bulk invariant.
summary: The paper analyzes the geometry of the Uhlmann phase generated when qubits interact with specific non-coherence-generating quantum channels. It demonstrates that this interaction creates localized vortex singularities in the parameter space, unlike previous models. This finding highlights a mechanism where environmental coupling generates measurable geometric phases through defect dynamics.
main_problem: The study investigates the geometry of the Uhlmann phase induced by quantum channels, contrasting this with previous analyses focused on thermal transitions driven by Hamiltonian variations.
main_result: A cyclically controlled non-coherence-generating channel induces a nontrivial Uhlmann phase characterized by local vortex–antivortex structures on the parameter torus. These defects nucleate and annihilate in pairs following a square-root coalescence law, contrasting with global winding number jumps.
method: The analysis uses Bloch-space geometry and calculates the Uhlmann phase via cyclic holonomy amplitudes derived from the channel parameters. Topological defect identification relies on solving for vanishing points of this amplitude.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using qubit systems undergoing evolution governed by a Non-Coherence-Generating (NCG) quantum channel, whose parameters drive the cycle in the space of CPTP maps.
key_observables: Uhlmann phase ($\Phi_U$), topological defects (vortices/antivortices), and the net topological charge.
important_parameters:
Channel parameters $(\mu, 
u, \chi)$, input-state orientation approaching critical values, and the parameter regime $	heta \in [\pi/3, 2\pi/3]$ for defect existence.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to NCG channels (Kraus rank two), and the initial state is assumed pure, carrying no intrinsic geometric phase.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows Bloch-vector trajectories tracing closed loops. Figure 2 maps $\Phi_U$ over the parameter cube, highlighting vortices at specific loci intersections. Figure 3 and 4 visualize these phase jumps and defect structures on the parameter torus.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by analyzing the Uhlmann phase geometry induced by NCG channels. It develops the mathematical framework using Bloch-space connections to locate singularities (vortices) in the channel parameter space, demonstrating their dynamics via coalescence laws while confirming zero net topological charge.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed geometric understanding of quantum information flow through noisy channels, offering insights into how environmental coupling (the channel parameters) can generate measurable geometric phases locally, which is crucial for designing robust quantum protocols.
